newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A broad front of dollar sellers helped the rand recapture a sizeable amount of lost ground against the U.S. currency in trade which ended Thursday with a whiff of burnt flesh in the air.

After sinking to yet another record low of 4.7670 against the dollar shortly after the official 0700 GMT opening, the rand rallied seven cents to touch a day's best of 4.6920 bid before settling 4.7020/7070.

Dealers said the currency was initially pummelled by a wave of importers looking to buy dollars at their month-ends. Coupled with small-scale offshore buying, the currency sank to its intraday low by 0713 GMT.
But by 0715 GMT, profit-taking by overseas and local banks who were long dollars triggered the start of the rand's retracement.

"There was a feeling that the market was overbought and some of the speculators started taking profits," a dealer said. The currency's retracement also triggered stop-loss dollar selling which aided its recovery.

"We saw a lot of selling from offshore," another trader said, adding that some players had been caught flat-footed by the speed of the currency's recovery. "There were a couple of burnt fingers out there."
"We may have scared away a few guys who though they could dictate this thing," another dealer added.
The profit-taking was accompanied by Reserve Bank intervention, which dealers described as successful. "It was not aggressive intervention, but the trend was his friend," one said.
By 0940 GMT, the rand had reached its day's best level of 4.6920 bid against the dollar where dealers said importer and offshore demand for dollars resurfaced.
"There is very good support for the dollar at 4.70 from local banks, importers and offshore (players)," a trader said.
Dealers said that in the short-term the currency was expected to retrace further, possibly to the 4.65 level.
"The trend has not reversed but things are not looking as bad as they have," the trader said, adding that the fact that the rand had managed to hold the bulk of its gains on the day was encouraging.
"There is no reason for it not to go back to 4.65...But there are still plenty of (dollar) longs out there and it just depends if they want to hold on to them or not," he said.

The rand also regained some of its lost composure against the British pound and the German mark. It was last quoted at 7.6429/6557 against sterling after touching a fresh low of 7.7824 earlier and at 0.3217/3222 marks after hitting a new low of 0.3166 in the morning.
Trade on the bond market was purely driven by the rand's movements.
The key R150 stock was last quoted at 15.93 percent, just off its intraday low of 15.925 percent and 16 basis points off its intraday high of 16.09 percent.
Dealers said foreigners had been the main sellers of local gilts on the day, while local institutions had absorbed stock on offer above the 16 percent level.
"The gilts were essentially driven by the rand...we were given quite a bit of stock by the foreigners but above 16 (percent) looks like a good level for the institutions," a dealer said.
He said the market appeared to have settled for the 16 percent as a strike level for options close-out next Thursday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners sold a net 471.79 million rand worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 476.21 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 9.81 billion rand from 8.12 billion rand on Tuesday.

On the money market, three-month NCD rates were slightly higher at between 16.30 and 16.40 offered from 16.20 to 16.40 previously, while the 90-day BA rate was slightly higher at between 15.85 and 15.70 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 8.667 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.722 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
